accounting_interpretation.finding: All three MaxRSS values are about 1.5 MiB above the binary 106 GiB value, and two AveRSS values are also near that value. The repeated ceiling-shaped values are consistent with a Slurm jobacct or cgroup-scoped measurement at the step limit, but the available interface cannot distinguish a censored cgroup peak from aggregate resident pages with sufficient confidence.
accounting_interpretation.reason: Direct SSH to compute nodes is denied. No extra Slurm step was created because that would perturb the running allocation. Therefore per-process RSS, memory.current, memory.peak, memory.events and kernel OOM counters were not read.
accounting_interpretation.oom_evidence: No terminal Slurm OOM state, nonzero exit code or stale scientific status was observed. This is absence of exposed evidence, not proof that memory.events oom/oom_kill counters are zero.

continuation_decision.basis: All three steps are live, have fresh status/checkpoint activity and expose no terminal failure. Interrupting them would discard healthy progress and would not improve the measurement. This is permission to preserve the current owners, not acceptance of a safe memory margin.
required_terminal_evidence: natural boundary or terminal step state
final uncensored peak or independently accepted explanation of the ceiling-shaped accounting value
no OOM or oom_kill event evidence when the existing owner can expose it without a new step

next_request_recommendation.basis: The observed 106 GiB peak may be censored at the present limit. A 128 GiB worker request is nominally 20.75 percent higher than that limit, but the true workload peak and therefore the real margin are unknown until another complete lifecycle is profiled. The 160/128/2 GiB allocation, worker and owner values are a candidate for independent admission review, not an accepted resource configuration.
next_request_recommendation.admission: Use the existing dispatcher, lock, Claims and rotation. Do not cancel healthy jobs or introduce a competing controller.
